oil.summary: Crude sold off hard on Friday, with WTI dropping 5.77% to $96.01/bbl and Brent losing 5.48% to $99.08/bbl, as Saudi Arabia's successful rerouting of exports through Ras Tanura defused the acute supply-shock narrative that had driven prices above $101 earlier in the week. With Saudi Aramco having sold up to 60 million barrels for September-October loadings via Persian Gulf ports rather than through the Strait of Hormuz—where tanker traffic slumped to just four vessels on Thursday—traders unwound Hormuz-risk premium aggressively. RBOB gasoline led the decline at -8.47%. On the geopolitical flank, the US Congress passed a sweeping sanctions bill targeting Russian and Iranian energy, threatening 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian crude including India, which pushed back publicly. Japanese refiners stated they hold sufficient crude stocks through November, limiting demand-side urgency.
drivers: Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura workaround—up to 60 mn bbls sold for Sep/Oct loadings—eases Hormuz supply-disruption premium, sending WTI and Brent sharply lower
Hormuz tanker traffic collapsed to just four vessels Thursday, but market focus shifted to rerouting success rather than strait closure risk
US Congress passes Russia/Iran energy sanctions bill with threatened 100% tariffs on Russian oil buyers; India warns of diplomatic fallout, adding medium-term flow-rerouting uncertainty

gas.summary: Natural gas markets were split on Friday. Henry Hub edged up just 0.28% to $2.909/MMBtu, extending a modest weekly gain of 2.76% with little sector-specific news driving the move. European TTF surged 3.96% to €79.375/MWh—up 25% on the month—with LNG supply disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz remaining the central concern; at least two LNG carriers have transited Hormuz this week, with others resorting to ship-to-ship transfers outside the strait, underscoring ongoing logistical strain for Qatar and UAE export flows. TotalEnergies and BlackRock's GIP separately announced a $1.8 billion partnership for African oil and gas assets, signalling continued upstream capital commitment. European gas price data warrants close monitoring given the scale of the monthly move.
drivers: Hormuz LNG disruption—only limited carrier transits and STS transfers this week—keeps European TTF elevated, up ~25% month-on-month
Henry Hub quiet at $2.909/MMBtu; no major domestic demand or supply catalysts identified in today's headlines
TotalEnergies/BlackRock $1.8bn African gas asset deal signals continued upstream investment appetite despite geopolitical volatility

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs gained 2.49% to $82.535/EUA on Friday, supported by TTF's sharp 3.96% daily rally to €79.375/MWh, which raises gas-fired generation costs and tightens carbon compliance economics. A notable structural signal came from India, where coal power generation flatlined in H1 2024 through H1 2026—the first two-year period of zero coal growth in over fifty years—reflecting the accelerating clean energy buildout. INEOS launched the EU's first full-scale carbon storage facility in Denmark, a milestone for European carbon abatement infrastructure. The US sanctions bill's uranium carve-out was flagged as notable, keeping nuclear supply chains insulated. News flow is moderate for the power sector today, but TTF strength and the EUA move are the dominant near-term pricing forces.
drivers: TTF +3.96% on the day lifts gas-fired generation costs, supporting EUA demand and pushing EU carbon up 2.49% to $82.54/EUA
INEOS opens EU's first full-scale CCS site in Denmark—structural step forward for European carbon abatement capacity
India's coal power generation records zero growth over two years for the first time in 50+ years, marking a clean-energy inflection with long-run carbon market implications
